observations: Lu et al., Scientific Reports 2024, instantiate latent-cause inference with a Bayesian nonparametric mechanism and context vectors in LCNet; Simulation 1 was repeated N=100 times and demonstrates shared-structure reuse with reduced catastrophic interference.
The paper explicitly reports that matching the sticky latent-cause prior to temporal autocorrelation was important for explaining blocked/interleaved human-learning effects.

Simulation 1 supplied a 128-dimensional context-indicative signal with 10% bit flips and deliberately kept it easy enough that latent-cause inference was guaranteed accurate; therefore that simulation is not evidence that LCNet's switch detector is robust under sparse/delayed ambiguous evidence.

The authors publish code for Simulations 1-2 at qihongl/LCNet. The public PECRP module identifies itself as an incremental sticky-CRP/Anderson-style clustering implementation with an existing-versus-new-cluster coupling prior; this run did not claim source-exact equivalence between that code and the synthetic detector below.

design.stream: Same nonlinear synthetic latent-stream family as prior run: ambient N=24, latent d=6, active rank k=4, T=900, two persistent task/representation changes plus two temporary task-relevant latent silences.
design.event_sparse_admission: A provisional lost decoder direction is considered only after persistent decoder mass leaves the active span and covariance energy along that direction drops. It is promoted to the two-slot dormant bank only after sustained low energy followed by residual-aligned energy reappearance. This is an engineering control, not a biological mechanism.
design.naive_control: Store lost decoder components whenever active-subspace rotation crosses a small mass threshold, capacity two.

release_controls.standardized_cusum: Heuristic standardized prequential-error CUSUM with weak unsupervised reconstruction-residual channel.
release_controls.sticky_latent_cause_screen: Two-state sticky HMM over binned standardized supervised surprise plus reconstruction-residual surprise. Emissions pooled on disjoint calibration streams from both tracker families; shared hazard=0.005, state persistence=0.92 and posterior release threshold=0.35. This is inspired by latent-cause inference, not an LCNet reproduction.

interpretation: The event-sparse gate cuts false-admission churn by roughly 82-86% versus naive lost-component storage across both trackers and feedback regimes, but it also discards most true silence-return admissions. Churn suppression therefore came mainly from conservative under-admission, not from a solved utility test.

Dormant-memory MSE versus plain tracking remains statistically unresolved under moderate feedback: PAST event-minus-plain mean -0.00896 with bootstrap95 [-0.02261, 0.00287]; Oja -0.00040 with [-0.01099, 0.00930]. There is no evidence here that the new admission gate improves task loss.

The shared sticky-HMM screen increases held-out switch detection under severe 40-step/25%-label feedback from 12.5% for the current CUSUM control to 41.7% PAST-like and 37.5% Oja-like. It also raises false releases modestly and has long median latency (99.5 and 74 steps). This is a promising direction, not a solved detector.

The unsupervised reconstruction-residual channel was weakly discriminative in pooled calibration; supervised surprise carried most of the switch signal. Merely adding a residual channel does not solve sparse/delayed release.

limits: Synthetic bounded audit; no source-exact SPLiT S8/S11/S12 reproduction and no claim about biological dormant-memory implementation.
Event-admission parameters and HMM settings were screened on disjoint synthetic calibration seeds but not nested-cross-validated across a broader environment family.
True/false admission labels use known synthetic silence windows and therefore evaluate the mechanism; they are not available to an online agent.
Sticky-HMM emissions are coarse binned surprise statistics rather than LCNet's published latent-cause likelihood model.
MSE scale is specific to this synthetic stream; compare paired methods, not absolute values.

candidate_update.positive_scope: A persistent lost-mass/energy-drop/reappearance gate greatly reduces micro-rotation memory churn. A tracker-shared sticky latent-cause posterior can recover more persistent changes than the current CUSUM under sparse delayed labels.
candidate_update.negative_boundary: Conservative event admission also misses most true returns and yields no resolved task-loss gain. The tested unsupervised residual statistic is too weak, and the sticky posterior remains slow with nontrivial false releases.

bounded_audit.exact_next_action: Keep retrying read-only PLOS Figshare Code.zip recovery without mutation. Replace the coarse binned sticky-HMM screen with a source-derived latent-cause/run-length posterior that models predictive likelihood directly and uses temporal autocorrelation as an explicit prior. On disjoint calibration environments, learn an unsupervised observation-change likelihood from covariance/subspace residual features rather than a single reconstruction-residual scalar. Lock parameters before held-out evaluation across PAST/GROUSE-like and Oja-like trackers, moderate/severe feedback, and altered switch/silence hazards. Use the cause posterior jointly for dormant-memory promotion and release so a direction is stored only when evidence favors temporary latent silence over persistent context change. Report task loss, bank churn, true/false admission, true/false release, latency, calibration and posterior reliability. Keep source scope bounded until SPLiT S1 code is recovered.
